name: Trencadís
summary: A surface of broken tile and china that is set in mortar on a curved wall, bench or roof. Antoni Gaudí and Josep Maria Jujol made it a free, colourful skin for Barcelona buildings.

philosophy.core_thesis: A broken tile is not waste: a wall of shards takes any curve, and the glaze colour of each piece joins into one bright surface.
design_principles: Break glazed tiles and plates with a hammer into pieces of 2 to 10 cm.
Set the pieces in a bed of wet mortar on a curved wall, a bench or a chimney.
Mix many colours in one field; place the pieces at random and keep the pattern loose.
Add shards of plates, bottle glass and cups, so that a few printed motifs appear.
Keep the glaze face outward; the sharp edges of the shards stay below the grout line.
Fill the gaps with a thin mortar joint of 3 to 5 mm and wipe the face clean.
Use the mosaic on a form that has a curve: a serpentine bench, a lizard, a dome or a chimney.
anti_patterns: A flat grid of square tiles in one colour
A regular, printed tile pattern with no breaks
Smooth, uncut ceramic with no shard edge
A sharp-edged tile that cuts the hand
Pieces of one colour that give a plain surface

form.shape: Curved benches, ridge ornaments, chimneys, finials, domed roofs, columns and sculptural animals that carry a skin of shards.
form.profile: A soft, flowing curve with no sharp corner; the surface is rough and bright, with small variations of 1 to 3 mm in the height of the shards.
form.foot_and_rim: Edges are rounded with mortar and the shards are cut to follow the curve; the top of a bench ends in a smooth lip.
form.proportion: Shards are 2 to 10 cm across; the mortar bed is 2 to 3 cm thick and the mosaic skin adds 10 to 15 mm to the wall.
rules: Apply the shards on a curve.
Use free colour in each field.
Break the tile by hand and keep the pieces large.
Do not place the shards in rows.

bodies.rule: Use the waste of tile factories and household china: glazed earthenware first, with porcelain and glass as a bright accent. The mortar base must be strong and curved.

forming.joins: Each shard is pressed into a bed of lime or cement mortar on the wall; the joint is thin and the same colour as the mortar.
forming.details: A small chip on the edge of a shard, a part of a printed flower or a letter on a plate, and a thin uneven mortar line.

glaze.pattern: Free fields of broken colour: blue, white, green, yellow and orange, with small parts of plate patterns, and some bright whole discs.
glaze.gloss: Gloss, about 70 to 95 GU; each shard gives its own sheen, and the whole surface glitters in the sun.
glaze.wear: The glaze keeps its colour in the sun and rain; a mortar joint may crack, and a loose shard falls off the edge.

palette.strategy: Many saturated colours in small pieces; each field has a leading colour, for example blue and white on one bench and orange and green on a roof.

firing.kiln: The shards come from many kilns: tile factories fire earthenware tile, and potters fire plate and cup shards at higher heat.
processes: firing of the tile at the factory
wiping and curing of the mortar
firing.scale: The benches and walls of Park Güell run for hundreds of metres; the work used teams of masons and many tonnes of waste tile.
firing.signs: Uneven shard edges, a patch of a plate motif, a thin mortar line and a bright, glittering face.

pieces.form: Serpentine bench wall covered in blue, white and yellow shards
Chimney top in a twist covered in white and green shards
Dragon-back roof ridge with scales of glazed shards
Cross finial with a base covered in shards of plates

positive: broken tile mosaic on a curved bench
trencadís surface in blue white and yellow
serpentine seat with a glittering face
pieces of plate patterns in the mosaic

canonical_works.maker: Antoni Gaudí and Josep Maria Jujol

emotion.target_response: Play and wonder: the viewer sees a wall that glitters like a toy and moves like a wave.

use_cases: a render of a Gaudí-style bench or roof
a mosaic design from waste tile
a label for broken ceramic architecture
avoid_when: the brief needs a flat, regular tile wall
the brief needs a clean, minimal surface
the brief needs a single bright glaze

modifiers.how: Replace the shards by whole roof tiles in a zigzag pattern and add a finial with an eosin glaze.
Remove the shards, use extruded hollow panels with a matt face and keep a straight joint.

ornament_level.note: The mosaic is a free pattern; low ornament breaks the style.

wall_thickness.note: The skin adds 10 to 25 mm of shard and mortar to the wall.
